title: Towns and cities
about: Collocations for describing towns and cities: what visitors enjoy, like cobbled streets, pavement cafés and good value, and the problems of big cities, like deprived areas, exhaust fumes and bumper-to-bumper traffic.

parts.title: Describing towns and cities for visitors
Towns and cities and their problems

items.pattern: the city skyline · a skyline of towers / domes / spires · noun + noun
items.meaning: the outline of a city's buildings against the sky, seen from a distance
items.example: From our hotel room we had a wonderful view of the **city skyline** at sunset.
more: Two huge cranes now stand out on the **city skyline**.
We took an evening boat trip on the river to photograph the **skyline** lit up at night.
items.watchOut: «Силует міста» — найчастіше the (city) skyline, одним словом. Silhouette англійською звучить природніше про темну фігуру людини чи предмета.

items.pattern: (narrow / busy) cobbled streets · a cobbled square / lane · cobbles, cobblestones
items.meaning: streets covered with small round stones set in a regular pattern, as in many old towns
items.example: We spent the morning wandering through the narrow **cobbled streets** around the cathedral.
more: The wheels of my suitcase made a terrible noise on the **cobbled streets**.
There's a little **cobbled square** behind the market where they sell flowers on Sundays.
items.watchOut: «Бруківка» — cobbles або cobblestones, «брукований» — cobbled. Paved означає просто «з твердим покриттям» (плитка, асфальт), тож paved streets — ще не обов'язково бруківка.

items.pattern: a conservation area · be in / live in a conservation area · noun + noun
items.meaning: a part of a town that is officially protected because of its history or old buildings, so they can't easily be changed or knocked down
items.example: The old town is a **conservation area**, so all the shops have traditional wooden signs instead of plastic ones.
more: Our street became a **conservation area** last year, and now we need permission to replace the windows.
A developer wanted to build a hotel by the harbour, but it's a **conservation area**, so the plans were rejected.
items.watchOut: Conservation тут — не «консервація» в банках (це canning, preserving), а охорона, збереження. Не плутай з conservative (консервативний). Про природу частіше кажуть nature reserve (заповідник).

items.pattern: quaint old buildings / houses / cottages · a quaint little village / shop
items.meaning: attractive because they are unusual and old-fashioned
items.example: The harbour is surrounded by **quaint old buildings** painted blue, pink and yellow.
more: We stayed above a **quaint little bookshop** in the old town.
My grandmother lives in a **quaint** village where everyone still knows the postman by name.
items.watchOut: Quaint — зазвичай позитивне слово: «милий, старосвітський». Не плутай зі strange чи weird (дивний). Про звичаї чи ідеї quaint іноді звучить іронічно — «старомодний».

items.pattern: upmarket shops / restaurants / hotels / area · go upmarket · ↔ downmarket · US upscale
items.meaning: expensive and aimed at people with money and expensive tastes
items.example: The old covered market is now full of **upmarket shops** that most locals can't afford.
more: For our anniversary we treated ourselves to a night in an **upmarket** hotel.
The town has a few **upmarket** restaurants, but most people eat at the market stalls.
items.watchOut: «Елітний» магазин, ресторан чи район — upmarket (UK) або upscale (US), зазвичай не elite: elite кажуть про людей і групи (elite athletes, the elite).

items.pattern: rather / a bit / quite pricey · pricey restaurants / hotels / taxis · informal · also spelt pricy
items.meaning: expensive (an informal word, often said with a slight complaint)
items.example: We love the seafood there, but it's one of the more **pricey restaurants** in town, so we only go for birthdays.
more: Taxis are rather **pricey** here, so most people take the tram.
The flat was a bit **pricey**, but it was right next to the beach.
items.watchOut: Pricey — розмовне «дорогувате». «Дорогий» у значенні ціни — не valuable (цінний) і не precious (дорогоцінний): про ресторан чи таксі так не кажуть.

items.pattern: overpriced restaurants / food / tickets · be overpriced · also over-priced
items.meaning: more expensive than they should be for what you get
items.uk: заклади із завищеними цінами; занадто дорого як на таку якість
items.example: The restaurants on the seafront are **overpriced**: you pay double for the view.
more: Six euros for a bottle of water? That's ridiculously **overpriced**.
The concert tickets were **overpriced**, and we could hardly see the stage.
items.watchOut: Overpriced — про товар чи заклад: the food is overpriced. Про людину, з якої взяли забагато грошей, кажуть overcharged: we were overcharged. Не the food was overcharged.

items.pattern: be / offer good value (for money) · great / excellent / better value
items.meaning: worth the money you pay for it
items.example: The hostel isn't fancy, but at twenty pounds a night it's **good value**.
more: The family ticket is **good value** if you've got three children.
The new budget airline **offers good value** if you only travel with hand luggage.
items.watchOut: Value тут незлічуване: it's good value, без артикля в британській англійській. Good price — про саму ціну (I got it at a good price), а good value — про те, що за ці гроші отримуєш багато. Не cheap value.

items.pattern: a relaxed / friendly / lively atmosphere · have / create an atmosphere
items.meaning: a calm, informal feeling in a place, where people feel comfortable and nobody hurries them
items.example: The little bar by the harbour has a **relaxed atmosphere**, with old sofas and soft music.
more: Our new office has a much more **relaxed atmosphere**: nobody wears a suit.
The wedding was small, with a **relaxed atmosphere** and a barbecue in the garden.
items.watchOut: Relaxed — невимушена, неформальна атмосфера; relaxing — та, що допомагає відпочити (a relaxing bath, a relaxing holiday). Про кафе чи бар природніше relaxed atmosphere. Наголос в atmosphere — на перший склад.

items.pattern: a street / road / avenue runs from A to B · runs north to south · runs along / beside sth
items.meaning: (of a street or road) goes in a particular direction or between two places
items.example: Bridge Road **runs from the old bridge to the beach**, so you can walk to the sea in ten minutes.
more: A narrow lane **runs** along the back of the houses.
The old railway line **runs** along the valley, and now it's a walking trail.
items.watchOut: Про вулицю, дорогу чи стежку кажуть runs (from … to …, along, beside) у Present Simple: the road runs — так вона розташована. The road is running звучить так, ніби дорога кудись біжить. У розмові можна сказати й goes.

items.pattern: be lined with shops / cafés / trees / people · shops line the street
items.meaning: having a row of shops (or trees, people…) along each side
items.uk: обабіч стоять магазини; уздовж вулиці тягнуться магазини
items.example: The road down to the beach is **lined with souvenir shops** and ice-cream stands.
more: Thousands of fans **lined** the streets to welcome the team home.
Our street is **lined with** cherry trees, and it looks amazing in April.
items.watchOut: Після lined найчастіше — прийменник with: lined with shops. «Вулиця забудована магазинами» — не built with shops, а lined with shops. Можна й з дієсловом: shops line the street.

items.pattern: lively bars / streets / nightlife / atmosphere · a lively town
items.meaning: full of people, energy and fun
items.example: We found a street full of **lively bars**, each with a different band playing.
more: It's a **lively** town in summer, but very quiet in winter.
The market is **liveliest** on Saturday mornings, when the farmers come into town.
items.watchOut: Lively читається /ˈlaɪvli/ — через «ай», як live у live music. «Жвавий» — lively, не living (той, що живе) і не alive (живий, не мертвий).

items.pattern: fashionable clubs / bars / restaurants / area · trendy (informal)
items.meaning: popular with stylish people at the moment
items.example: My cousin got us onto the guest list at one of the city's most **fashionable clubs**.
more: Ten years ago nobody went there, but now it's a **fashionable** area full of art galleries.
We couldn't get a table at the **fashionable** new restaurant, so we had pizza instead.
items.watchOut: «Модний» — fashionable або trendy. Modern — «сучасний», без відтінку моди: a modern club — просто новий, сучасний за дизайном.

items.pattern: a pavement café (UK) · a sidewalk café (US) · sit at a pavement café
items.meaning: cafés with tables outside on the pavement
items.uk: вуличні кафе зі столиками на тротуарі
items.example: We had lunch at a **pavement café** and watched people go by.
more: The **pavement cafés** in the square put their tables out in April.
It was too cold to sit outside, so the **pavement cafés** were empty.
items.watchOut: Pavement у британській англійській — тротуар (американською sidewalk), а не дорожнє покриття. «Літнє кафе» зі столиками надворі — pavement café; summer café англійською звучить незвично.

items.pattern: a tree-lined avenue / street / road · the street is lined with trees
items.meaning: wide streets with trees along both sides
items.example: My grandparents live on a quiet **tree-lined avenue** near the park.
more: In autumn the **tree-lined** streets of the old district turn red and gold.
We walked from the station to the castle along a **tree-lined road**.
items.watchOut: Порядок слів: tree-lined (дерево + lined), з дефісом, перед іменником: a tree-lined street. Після дієслова — the street is lined with trees. Не lined-tree і не trees-lined.

items.pattern: a residential area / district / street / neighbourhood
items.meaning: parts of a town where people live, with houses or flats rather than offices, shops or factories
items.example: It's a quiet **residential area**, so there's nowhere to buy food after eight.
more: Lorries aren't allowed in **residential streets** at night.
We moved to a **residential district** on the edge of town when the kids were born.
items.watchOut: «Спальний (житловий) район» — найчастіше a residential area, не a sleeping district і не a living area (living area — зона відпочинку в квартирі). Про ціле містечко, звідки їздять на роботу, британці ще кажуть dormitory town.

items.pattern: high-rise flats / blocks / buildings · a high-rise · a tower block
items.meaning: tall blocks of flats with many floors
items.example: From the train you can see rows of **high-rise flats** on the edge of the city.
more: Some people love living in a **high-rise**, but I'd miss having a garden.
They knocked down the old **high-rise blocks** and built low houses with gardens.
items.watchOut: «Багатоповерхівка» — a high-rise (block of flats) або a tower block, не a many-floor house. Multi-storey кажуть найчастіше про паркінг: a multi-storey car park. Flats — британське слово, американці кажуть apartments.

items.pattern: the inner city · inner-city areas / schools / problems (з дефісом перед іменником)
items.meaning: the poorer areas near the centre of a big city, where there are often social problems
items.uk: бідні, неблагополучні райони біля центру міста
items.example: My uncle is a doctor in the **inner city**, and many of his patients can't afford healthy food.
more: The charity runs free football clubs for kids in **inner-city areas**.
The council has promised more money for housing in the **inner city**.
items.watchOut: Inner city — не просто «центр міста» (це city centre / town centre): у слові є відтінок бідності й соціальних проблем. Про центр із магазинами й музеями кажи city centre.

items.pattern: an imposing building / entrance / gate / castle
items.meaning: big and impressive, making people feel small or respectful
items.example: The museum is an **imposing building** with huge stone columns at the entrance.
more: At the end of the drive stood an **imposing** old house with forty windows.
The bank's head office is an **imposing** glass tower right next to the river.
items.watchOut: Imposing — величний, що вражає розміром. Не плутай з дієсловом impose (нав'язувати): an imposing building — не «нав'язлива будівля». Про людину, яку щось вразило, кажуть impressed, а про будівлю — imposing або impressive.

items.pattern: an urban wasteland · a stretch / patch of wasteland · waste ground
items.meaning: an empty area of a city in bad condition, with nothing useful on it
items.example: Twenty years ago this park was an **urban wasteland** full of broken glass.
more: After the factories closed, the whole riverside became an **urban wasteland**.
Volunteers turned a patch of **wasteland** behind the station into a community garden.
items.watchOut: «Пустир» — wasteland або waste ground, не empty place. Desert — пустеля з піском; про місто так кажуть хіба образно.

items.pattern: a no-go area / zone · become a no-go area
items.meaning: a place so dangerous that people, and even the police, are afraid to go there
items.uk: небезпечний район, куди ніхто не наважується потикатися
items.example: Ten years ago the estate was a **no-go area**, but now families walk their dogs there.
more: Our guide warned us that parts of the port are **no-go areas** after dark.
Locals say the park became a **no-go area** when the street lights stopped working.
items.watchOut: No-go area — найчастіше про місце, куди бояться ходити через злочинність. Якщо туди просто не пускають (військова зона, місце аварії), природніше restricted area або exclusion zone. Пишеться з дефісом.

items.pattern: be strewn with litter / rubbish / leaves / clothes · strew – strewed – strewn
items.meaning: with litter lying all over it in an untidy way
items.example: After the fair, the whole field was **strewn with litter**.
more: My son's bedroom floor is always **strewn with** clothes and comics.
In October the paths in the park are **strewn with** leaves.
items.watchOut: Litter — сміття, яке кидають на вулиці (папірці, банки, пляшки); rubbish — сміття загалом. Обидва незлічувані: litter, не litters. Strewn — третя форма від strew.

items.pattern: run-down buildings / areas / hotels / flats · an area is run-down
items.meaning: in very bad condition because nobody has repaired or looked after them
items.example: Half the shops on the high street are empty, and the **run-down buildings** make the whole town look sad.
more: They bought a **run-down** farmhouse and spent five years fixing it up.
My first flat was in a **run-down** block with no lift and damp walls.
items.watchOut: Run-down — з дефісом перед іменником: a run-down hotel. Не плутай з run out (закінчитися) і run over (переїхати). Про людину run-down означає «виснажений, змучений».

items.pattern: a deprived area / neighbourhood / family / childhood · deprivation
items.meaning: areas where people don't have enough money, good housing, jobs or services for a decent life
items.example: The new library is in one of the most **deprived areas** of the city.
more: Children from **deprived** families get free school meals.
She grew up in a **deprived** neighbourhood but became the first doctor in her family.
items.watchOut: Deprived — бідний, позбавлений нормальних умов життя. Не плутай з depraved (розбещений, аморальний): одна літера — і зовсім інше значення.

items.pattern: an industrial zone / area / estate
items.meaning: parts of a city with factories and warehouses rather than homes
items.example: The new furniture warehouse is in the **industrial zone** just outside town, so you need a car to get there.
more: My dad works at a bakery on the **industrial estate** near the motorway.
The river used to be dirty because of the **industrial zone** upstream.
items.watchOut: Industrial — промисловий; industrious — працьовитий (про людину). «Промзона» — industrial zone або industrial area, у Британії часто industrial estate.

items.pattern: a sprawling city / suburb / estate · urban sprawl
items.meaning: spread out over a very large area, often in an untidy way (slightly negative)
items.example: Los Angeles is a **sprawling city** where almost everyone drives.
more: The village has turned into a **sprawling** suburb of identical houses.
**Sprawling** shopping centres outside town have killed many small shops in the centre.
items.watchOut: Big / large city — нейтрально. Sprawling додає відтінок: місто безладно розрослося на величезну територію, і без машини там важко. Sprawled кажуть про людину, що розлеглася: sprawled on the sofa.

items.pattern: bumper-to-bumper traffic · the road is bumper to bumper · also nose-to-tail traffic
items.meaning: so many cars so close together that they almost touch and move very slowly
items.uk: суцільний затор, машини стоять впритул одна до одної
items.example: There was **bumper-to-bumper traffic** on the way to the coast, so the trip took five hours.
more: The bridge is **bumper to bumper** every morning at half past eight.
A crash on the motorway left drivers in **bumper-to-bumper traffic** for miles.
items.watchOut: «Пробка, затор» — a traffic jam, не a cork. Bumper-to-bumper описує, як щільно стоять машини: перед іменником з дефісами (bumper-to-bumper traffic), після дієслова — без них (the road was bumper to bumper). Британці ще кажуть nose-to-tail.

items.pattern: exhaust fumes · traffic fumes · breathe in (the) fumes
items.meaning: the harmful gas that comes out of the back of cars, buses and lorries
items.example: In summer the **exhaust fumes** on the main road make my eyes sting.
more: Children walking to school breathe in **exhaust fumes** from all the cars waiting outside.
The new low-emission zone should cut **exhaust fumes** in the city centre.
items.watchOut: «Вихлопні гази» — exhaust fumes, не exhausted gases: exhausted — виснажений, змучений. Fumes зазвичай у множині. Вимова /ɪɡˈzɔːst/: h не читається.

items.pattern: the volume of traffic · traffic volume · heavy / light traffic
items.meaning: the amount of traffic on the roads
items.example: The **volume of traffic** in the centre has fallen since parking became so expensive.
more: The road was built for a much smaller **volume of traffic**.
The **volume of traffic** doubles in summer when the tourists arrive.
items.watchOut: Traffic незлічуване: the volume / amount of traffic, не the number of traffic (але the number of cars). «Інтенсивний рух» — heavy traffic, не strong чи big traffic.

items.pattern: the incessant roar of traffic / engines / planes · incessant noise / rain / complaints
items.meaning: a very loud, deep noise that never stops
items.example: Living near the airport means putting up with the **incessant roar** of planes.
more: After a week in the mountains, the **incessant roar** of the city was a shock.
I'm tired of my brother's **incessant** complaints about his job.
items.watchOut: Incessant — безперервний і зазвичай дратівливий: incessant noise / rain / complaints. Roar — гучний гуркіт, рев (двигунів, моря, натовпу); звичайний шум — noise. «Сильний дощ» — heavy rain, не strong rain.

items.pattern: comfortable / leafy / quiet suburbs · live in the suburbs
items.meaning: pleasant areas on the edge of a city where people with enough money live, and from where they travel into the city to work
items.example: Most of the people in my office live in the **comfortable suburbs** and take the train into town.
more: We live in the **suburbs**, so it takes me forty minutes to get to work.
The **comfortable suburbs** are only twenty minutes from the shanty towns, but they feel like a different world.
items.watchOut: Suburbs — передмістя, звідки щодня їздять на роботу в місто, часто заможні. Outskirts — просто край, околиці міста. Живуть in the suburbs, не on the suburbs. Наголос на перший склад.

items.pattern: a shanty town · a shanty (= a hut)
items.meaning: areas of very poor homes made from things like tin, cardboard and plastic, usually on the edge of a big city
items.uk: нетрі; квартали халуп із підручних матеріалів
items.example: Thousands of families have built a **shanty town** on the hills above the city.
more: The charity builds clean water points in **shanty towns** around the capital.
Twenty years ago this was a **shanty town**; now it has proper houses, a school and a clinic.
items.watchOut: Shanty town — халупи з підручних матеріалів (жерсть, картон, пластик). Slums — ширше слово: будь-які нетрі, також у старих кам'яних будинках. Не плутай shanty і shabby (обшарпаний).

warmup.uk: Сувеніри біля замку надто дорогі — вони того не варті.
warmup.q: The souvenirs near the castle are ___.
warmup.explain: Overpriced — про товар чи заклад із завищеною ціною. Overcharged — про людину, з якої взяли забагато: we were overcharged.

warmup.uk: Ми живемо в тихому спальному районі.
warmup.q: We live in a quiet ___ area.
warmup.explain: Житловий, «спальний» район — a residential area. Living area — зона відпочинку в квартирі.

warmup.uk: Вона викладає в школі в бідному районі біля центру міста.
warmup.q: She teaches at a school in the ___ city.
warmup.explain: The inner city — бідні райони біля центру із соціальними проблемами. Просто центр міста — the city centre.

warmup.uk: Мій брат ходить лише в модні клуби.
warmup.q: My brother only goes to ___ clubs.

warmup.uk: Ми годину стояли в суцільному заторі.
warmup.q: We sat in ___ traffic for an hour.
warmup.explain: Машини стоять впритул одна до одної — bumper-to-bumper traffic. Просто затор — a traffic jam.

warmup.uk: Від вихлопних газів у мене болить голова.
warmup.q: The ___ fumes give me a headache.
warmup.explain: Вихлопні гази — exhaust fumes. Exhausted — виснажений, змучений.

warmup.uk: Таксі тут — вигідний варіант, якщо вас четверо.
warmup.q: A taxi here is good ___ if there are four of you.
warmup.explain: Варте своїх грошей — good value (for money), без артикля.

warmup.uk: На цій вулиці багато дорогих елітних магазинів.
warmup.q: There are lots of ___ shops on this street.
warmup.explain: Дорогі, «елітні» магазини — upmarket (US upscale). Elite кажуть про людей: elite athletes.

A.q: The old fishing village is now a ___ area, so its cottages will look the same in a hundred years.
A.explain: Conservation area — охоронна історична зона. Conservative — консервативний.

A.q: Our favourite ___ café has six little tables right next to the fountain.
A.explain: Кафе зі столиками на тротуарі — pavement café (американською sidewalk café).

A.q: The ___ gates of the palace are ten metres high.
A.explain: Imposing — величний. Impressed — вражений (про людину), imposed — нав'язаний.

B.q: The government has promised new jobs for the most ___ parts of the country.
B.explain: Deprived — бідний, неблагополучний. Depraved — розбещений, а deprivated — такого слова немає.

B.q: Don't walk barefoot here: the path is ___ with broken glass.
B.explain: Be strewn with — бути всипаним чимось. Strew – strewed – strewn.

B.q: It's a ___ city: it takes two hours to drive from one side to the other.
B.explain: A sprawling city — розлоге місто, що безладно розрослося. Spreaded — такої форми немає: spread – spread – spread.

practice.q: Five new towers have gone up since I was a child, so the city ___ looks completely different now.
Every postcard of the town shows the same ___: the castle, the bridge and two church towers against a blue sky.
The streets in the old town are ___: they're made of small round stones that get slippery when it rains.
Cars aren't allowed on the narrow cobbled ___ of the old town, so everyone walks or cycles.
We'd like to put solar panels on the roof, but our house is in a ___ area, so the council has said no.
The old mill district is a conservation ___, so none of its brick buildings can be knocked down.
We rented a ___ little cottage with a thatched roof and roses round the door. It was beautifully kept and looked like something from a children's picture book.
The village has kept its ___ old shops, like the tiny baker's with a bow window and a bell over the door.
The area has gone ___: the cheap cafés have closed, and now there are designer shops and wine bars.
My aunt only buys clothes in ___ shops, where a single scarf can cost two hundred pounds.
The cafés on the main square are a bit ___, so we usually bring a picnic.
We loved the food, but the hotel restaurant was rather ___, so after the first night we ate in town.

example.title: A weekend in the old town
example.uk:
Минулої весни ми з сестрою провели вихідні в старому портовому місті. Наше таксі з аеропорту годину стояло в суцільному заторі, і від вихлопних газів мене розбирав кашель. Ми проїхали повз ряди багатоповерхівок, а потім раптом з'явилося старе місто з брукованими вулицями й мальовничими старовинними будиночками.

Першого вечора ми сиділи у вуличному кафе на головній площі. Їжа була чудова, але дорогувата, тож наступного дня ми знайшли невеличкий заклад на бічній вуличці, де було значно вигідніше й панувала невимушена атмосфера.

Увечері в гавані було повно жвавих барів. Ми танцювали до другої ночі, а дорогою назад до готелю силует міста з мосту здавався чарівним.
example.en:
Last spring my sister and I spent a weekend in an old port city. Our taxi from the airport sat in [[bumper-to-bumper traffic|b8]] for an hour, and the [[exhaust fumes|b9]] made me cough. We drove past rows of [[high-rise flats|a17]], and then suddenly the old town appeared, with its [[cobbled streets|a2]] and [[quaint old buildings|a4]].

On the first evening we sat at a [[pavement café|a14]] on the main square. The food was lovely but rather [[pricey|a6]], so the next day we found a little place in a side street that was much [[better value|a8]] and had a [[relaxed atmosphere|a9]].

At night the harbour was full of [[lively bars|a12]]. We danced until two, and on our way back to the hotel the [[city skyline|a1]] looked magical from the bridge.
